title: napkin script 1, the object form
description: A script as JSON: an array of instructions, each an object naming its verb. Generated from the verb table by npm run api-docs; validateScript is the full check.

expression.description: An expression, its source without the parentheses: { "expr": "20 + i * 40" }.

color.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

run.description: A run of a text: from start to end (not included), and the character attributes it has.

highlight.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

color.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

position.description: Where a parsed instruction came from. A program building JSON leaves it out.

napkin.title: napkin
napkin.description: The language version the script was written for. The first line of a script; without it version 1 is assumed, with a warning.

page.title: page
page.description: The page size: a named size (a3, a4, a5, letter, legal, tabloid, square, slide, napkin) or a width and a height, turned portrait or landscape.

background.title: background
background.description: The page color, or none for a transparent page.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

name.title: name
name.description: The page's name, and the file stem it is written under.

units.title: units
units.description: The unit bare numbers are read in from here on: px, in, mm or pt. Pixels until changed.

seed.title: seed
seed.description: The seed for the hand-drawn pass. One script and one seed draw the same bytes every run.

newpage.title: newpage
newpage.description: Starts another page the same size, carrying the paint state across.

layer.title: layer
layer.description: A drawing layer. Marks after it go on it until the next layer.

group.title: group
group.description: A group layer. The layer and group lines in its block become its children.

clip.title: clip
clip.description: A clip group: everything its block draws shows only inside the block's last closed shape, in paint order, which paints nothing while it clips - the app's Make Clipping Mask. Without a closed shape in it, the block is a plain group.

tool.title: tool
tool.description: The kind of mark: pen (the app's Brush; brush is taken for it), marker (translucent, so overlapping passes build up like ink), copic (a broad, angled nib), pencil (a lead through the paper's grain; pencil picks one) or eraser (cuts its line's swath out of the marks drawn before it on its layer, as the app's Eraser does, and draws nothing of its own).

color.title: color
color.description: The ink color of every mark after it.
A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

width.title: width
width.description: The stroke width of every mark after it.

opacity.title: opacity
opacity.description: The opacity of every mark after it, from 0 to 1.

fill.title: fill
fill.description: The fill color of closed shapes after it, or none.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

gradient.title: gradient
gradient.description: A gradient fill for closed shapes after it: linear at an angle, or radial from the centre out, or none.

stroke.title: stroke
stroke.description: Turns the outline on or off. With it off, a closed shape is its fill alone.

style.title: style
style.description: The outline's dash: solid, dashed or dotted.

profile.title: profile
profile.description: How the width runs along a brush or marker stroke: uniform, rounded, tapered or wave.

nib.title: nib
nib.description: The angle of the copic nib, in degrees.

pencil.title: pencil
pencil.description: Takes up the Pencil at a grade: graphite alone, 9H to 9B, or charcoal (HB to 6B), compressed (2B to 6B) or vine (hard, medium, soft) and its grade. Every mark after it is drawn with that lead through the paper's grain, in its tone - or in the color given, a colored pencil. The width is the line's own; the app's softer leads draw broader at one tool width.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

rough.title: rough
rough.description: The hand-drawn pass for every mark after it: 0 is exact, 1 is clearly drawn by hand, and off is 0. Seeded, so it draws the same way every run.

font.title: font
font.description: The font family and size of text after it.

character.title: character
character.description: The character attributes of text after it: its face, tracking, kerning, leading, word spacing, capitals, scales, baseline shift, turn and highlight, and whether it is a superscript or a subscript, underlined or struck through. reset puts every one back.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

paragraph.title: paragraph
paragraph.description: The paragraph attributes of text after it: its alignment, its indents, the space before and after it, whether it hyphenates, and a bulleted or numbered list at a level. reset puts every one back.

textconfig.title: textconfig
textconfig.description: Defines a Text Configuration, a vector editor's Character Style: a named set of character attributes the book keeps, which text follows with config and its runs with config in their clauses. What a text has of its own overrides it. Defined again under its name, it changes for every text that follows it.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().
A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

accent.title: accent
accent.description: A Clean Language Accent for the next text: its paragraphs are colored as a language reads them - keywords, strings, numbers, comments, names - live as the app edits them. A language by its id or a name highlight.js knows it by (a name no word spells in quotes, "c++"), auto for the one the code reads most like, or none. It waits for the next text; one nothing takes is reported.

rect.title: rect
rect.description: A rectangle, with rounded corners when r is given.

circle.title: circle
circle.description: A circle, drawn as four cubic curves rather than a polygon.

ellipse.title: ellipse
ellipse.description: An ellipse, from its centre and two radii.

line.title: line
line.description: A straight line between two points.

polygon.title: polygon
polygon.description: A closed shape through a list of points, with rounded corners when r is given.

polyline.title: polyline
polyline.description: An open line through a list of points.

star.title: star
star.description: A star with the given number of points, between an outer and an inner radius.

arc.title: arc
arc.description: An open arc of a circle between two angles, in degrees clockwise from three o'clock.

spiral.title: spiral
spiral.description: A spiral winding out from its centre to the radius over the given number of turns.

shape.title: shape
shape.description: A named shape from the built-in library, drawn in a box from x, y. With one size its longer side is that long and it keeps its proportions; with a width and a height it is stretched to fill them.

wipe.title: wipe
wipe.description: Combines the marks its block draws, as the app's Wipe Stacks do, and draws what is left in their place: in (Wipe In, their union), out-front (Subtract Top from Below: the bottom one less the rest), out-back (Subtract Below from Top: the top one less the rest), mid (Mid Wipe: where all of them overlap), outer (Outer Wipes: where an odd number overlap) or clean (Clean Wipe: every piece of their overlaps, a mark each). What is left is painted as the topmost mark, or as the bottom one for out-front; text, pictures and eraser marks in the block are passed over. The block keeps its paint and transforms to itself, as a group does, and effects written just before it go on what it leaves.

stack.title: stack
stack.description: Stacks the marks its block draws as the app's Shape Stacker does, at the pieces under its points - the places where the marks overlap and where they do not: merge makes those pieces one shape, painted as the topmost mark over the first point, and each mark keeps what was not merged; remove takes them away from every mark. Text, pictures and eraser marks in the block are passed over. The block keeps its paint and transforms to itself, as a group does, and the points are where the stack line is.

path.title: path
path.description: One mark, from SVG path data or from a block of path steps. Each subpath of a compound path is one piece of the same mark.

move.title: move
move.description: Starts a new subpath at a point.

to.title: to
to.description: A straight segment to a point.

by.title: by
by.description: A straight segment by an offset from the current point.

curve.title: curve
curve.description: A cubic curve to a point, steered by two handles.

smooth.title: smooth
smooth.description: A cubic curve whose first handle mirrors the last one, so the join stays smooth.

through.title: through
through.description: A smooth curve through a list of points. Inside a path block it continues the subpath; outside one it is an open mark of its own.

close.title: close
close.description: Closes the current subpath back to its start.

split.title: split
split.description: Cuts the topmost mark drawn so far whose path passes within 4 px of a point, where the point lands on it, as the app's Split does: an open path becomes two, a closed one opens there, and a compound shape gives up the ring that was cut, as an open mark of its own. Nothing moves, and the pieces take the mark's place on its layer. In a wipe or a stack block it cuts among the marks the block has drawn.

smear.title: smear
smear.description: A pass of the Smear, a blending stump, along a list of points: it spreads the graphite of every pencil mark drawn so far that it reaches, along the drag, as the app's Smear does. The width is the stump's, scaled by the transform as a width is, and the strength from 0 to 1. In a wipe or a stack block it smears among the marks the block has drawn.

warp.title: warp
warp.description: Liquify's Warp, as the app's Liquify does it: a brush pushed from the point by dx and dy, carrying what is under its centre the whole way, like clay. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

twirl.title: twirl
twirl.description: Liquify's Twirl: turns what is under a brush at the point about its centre, by the angle in degrees there - clockwise on the screen, as rotate turns - and less toward the rim, so distances from the centre are kept. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

pucker.title: pucker
pucker.description: Liquify's Pucker: draws what is under a brush at the point in toward its centre, a point near the centre by the amount, 0 to 1, of its distance. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

bloat.title: bloat
bloat.description: Liquify's Bloat: pushes what is under a brush at the point out from its centre, a point near the centre by the amount, 0 to 1, of its distance. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

push.title: push
push.description: Saves the transform, the paint state and the units, for the next pop to restore.

pop.title: pop
pop.description: Restores the transform, the paint state and the units the last push saved.

rotate.title: rotate
rotate.description: Turns everything drawn after it, clockwise in degrees, about the origin or a point given with at.

scale.title: scale
scale.description: Scales everything drawn after it, about the origin or a point given with at. One factor scales both ways.

mirror.title: mirror
mirror.description: Reflects everything drawn after it: x swaps left and right across a vertical line, y swaps top and bottom across a horizontal one, at 0 unless given.

let.title: let
let.description: Names a number for the expressions after it, in the current units.

define.title: define
define.description: Records a block of drawing under a name without drawing it, for place to draw.

place.title: place
place.description: Draws a definition, moved, scaled or turned.

repeat.title: repeat
repeat.description: Runs a block a number of times, counting from 0 in the name given with as.

text.title: text
text.description: A text item, set and aligned, and editable in the app: Sideless Typing from its anchor, Sheet Typing in a box or inside a shape, or Path Typing along a path, set in its runs' styles, the whole of it following a Text Configuration with config. With markdown its text is Markdown, shown as it renders: Markdown Flow. With as marks the letters are drawn as brush strokes instead.

image.title: image
image.description: Places an image: an asset the host supplied, by name, or a data URL. Nothing is read from disk.

link.title: link
link.description: Places a linked file: one selectable element that references the file instead of drawing its contents into the page.

use.title: use
use.description: Copies in a document the host supplied, as a group, with its layers and anchors.

effect.title: effect
effect.description: An effect for the next layer, group or mark the script makes: a CSS filter function - blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, grayscale, sepia, invert, hue-rotate, opacity or drop-shadow, which is Outer Shadow - an appearance effect - feather, bevel, emboss, inner-shadow, outer-glow or inner-glow - or splatter, a vector editor's Scribble, which draws a mark's fill as a loose hatch (on a layer or a group it draws nothing) - or warp, a vector editor's Warp, which bends what takes it by a style, a layer's or a group's marks as one - or extrude and revolve, a vector editor's Classic 3D, which build a mark in depth and draw it as shaded faces (on a layer or a group they draw nothing). Any of them also takes `on fill` or `on stroke`, to work on that part of a mark alone, and `hidden`, to be kept without being drawn. Several stack in order, and none clears what is waiting.

anyOf.description: A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().
A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().
A CSS color: a name, #rgb to #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla().

blend.title: blend
blend.description: How the next layer or group the script makes mixes with what is drawn under it, the page's background included: a Napkin Blend by its name or by Illustrator's - stack or multiply, sheer or screen, cover or luminosity. A blend is a layer's, so it waits for the next layer or group; normal sets one back.

crop.title: crop
crop.description: The box every output is cut to: auto fits the ink with room to spare, none keeps the page, or a box given outright.

registration.title: registration
registration.description: One box every page is written in, so frames drawn by one script line up when they are played in sequence.
